message:
release: 0.2.154 -- the picture no longer stops every second when the wire cap is on

Since 0.2.148 the hard wire cap sent each periodic IDR at the capped rate, so a 30-140 KB keyframe
held the next frames for 0.25-0.58 s; on hardware encoders that clamp the GOP to about one second
(the user's office PC: requested 120, read back 30) that was a stop every 1-1.7 s. 0.2.147 had no cap
and no stop (user field check, 2026-10-08).
stutter-keyframe (t-jytruuim, 126f702): the periodic key period is at least 10 s on encoders that
honour it; an encoder whose own IDRs keep arriving well inside the policy period AND whose GOP
readback is below the request is latched as clamping, and only its own IDRs may go out at up to
max(R, min(4R, 12 Mbps)) under one 2 s moving-window ledger (2r + one datagram) shared by original,
FEC and NACK replay -- no refund, no free credit across epochs or reconnects, no grant after recent
loss. Forced-key recovery keeps a bounded retry instead of a latch on a refused ForceKeyFrame.
Verified: Codex SOURCE OK on 26ce462 (+ test-only 126f702); verifier's independent Release builds
and the main integration build -- build gate (no test seam in the shipped exe), burst ledger and
sender-admission tests (bypass mutations fail the same bound), fec lossless no-premature-NACK 3/3,
recovery, punch, resume, udp_control. Measured on a clamp emulation at 1.5 Mbps: >250 ms stops 11 -> 1.
Known flaky, pre-existing: host_encode_epoch_test (b7c9164-equivalent 2/20 vs this 1/20 under GPU
contention) and host_wire_cap_defer_test (fails only right after builds; 0/20 for both interleaved).
Not verified: the office PC's real encoder detection and feel -- that is the user's field check.

Product: version only (PC 0.2.153 -> 0.2.154; APK stays 0.2.26). Test: none. Docs: none.
